gap: No result ChatGPT got states, on a common basis across models, what each maker's 'tilt' figure measures (one-direction tilt from vertical vs the total swing, and '90° left and right' on the L-GL4D4 Ultra) or which wattage and lumen figure goes with it; I could not source that comparison this session, so it is not a sourced gap yet.
standout_why: I could not open any of the cited rival pages. All lumarysmart.com URLs (the 9W, the RGBAI Pro and the 90° eyeball), Wayfair and cloudybaylighting.com returned HTTP 429. Both Best Buy pages timed out, manuals.plus returned 403 and Walmart showed a bot wall. The one page I read, lumaryusa.com's 9W listing, repeats what ChatGPT's cited lumarysmart.com page for the same light already showed: 810 lm, 40° tilt, 45° beam, CRI 90. Its only extra items are a 25,000-hour rated life and 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi plus Bluetooth. Those are small additions, and I could not check whether the rival pages also carry them.
decides: Nothing yet. The finding that could change the pick is whether Lumary's '90° tilt' on the Ultra and Pro and '40° tilt' on the 9W measure the same thing. A search snippet for the L-GL4D4 manual on manuals.plus says '90° left and right adjustment' and '100° luminous angle', but I did not open that page, so it cannot go on the page. If a rerun confirms that wording, the 90° models may aim much further than the 9W figures suggest, which favours them for sloped ceilings and artwork. Until then, keep ChatGPT's order and the current page's picks unchanged.
